name: Somerton Man (Tamam Shud) code, Adelaide, 1948
ciphertext_source: Cipherbrain post 5 (Schmeh 2018, sources/schmeh/posts/05-somerton.txt) and Wikipedia 'Somerton Man' (fetched 24 Sept 2026); Wikipedia reads the first letters of lines 1 and 3 as W, Schmeh as M; an 'x' sits above line 4. Faint pencil indentations on the back cover of a 1941 Whitcombe & Tombs (NZ) FitzGerald Rubaiyat; the book itself is lost, only police photographs survive.
alphabet: Latin capitals, 12 distinct letters over 50 characters

constraints.identification: Carl 'Charles' Webb (1905-1948), Abbott and Fitzpatrick, 26 July 2022, DNA; coroner's formal finding still pending July 2026
constraints.prior_analysis: Turnbull and Bihari 2009, Abbott's group 2009-14: letter statistics fit English word initials, not a substitution cipher
constraints.not_a_cipher: treated as an initialism; the plaintext, if any, is a sentence whose word initials are these letters

cheap_test_done: Cheap test 3, 24 Sept 2026 (specs/cheap-tests/somerton_rubaiyat.py, .out): the five lines and every substring of 5+ letters searched against the word-initial sequence of FitzGerald's Rubaiyat (Gutenberg #246, first and fifth editions with FitzGerald's preface and notes, 12,180 words). Line 5 contains a 7-letter run TSAMSTG that equals the initials of 'the Son, and Malik Shah the Grandson' in FitzGerald's preface (line 34 of the Gutenberg body); the flanking letters (ITTM before, AB after) do not continue the match (the host reads TAA...OTB). Control: 1000 random five-line sets drawn from the English initial-letter distribution, same search: longest run 5 in 335 sets, 6 in 25, 7 or more in 0 of 1000. This is a search result, not a reading: a 7-of-13 partial match in a preface, and the 1941 NZ edition may not print that preface.
cheap_tests_in_order: 1. Establish what the 1941 Whitcombe & Tombs edition contains (preface or not; which FitzGerald edition) from a library catalogue or a scan on Trove/IA; if it carries the preface, rerun test 3 on that exact text and on each quatrain separately. Cost $2, Sonnet.

2. Webb's own texts: Abbott's group reported poetry in Webb's possession and his known letters; run the initials search over any published text of his. Cost $2 once a text exists; otherwise an ASKS row.
3. Initialism generation is not a cheap test (the space is open-ended): do not run a solver. A candidate sentence is judged only by initials_regex plus the English gate.
matched_control: random initial strings from English prose, as in cheap test 3
value: very high in fame, low in verifiability: no key source can grade any sentence above M
status_24_Sept_2026: open; not a cipher by consensus; identification of the man does not read the letters
schema_note: cheap_tests_in_order are proposals (rule 10: an approach is not a claim); a test actually run is under cheap_test_done with its control
